newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds firm, gear up for positive data.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds firm, gear up for positive data.

text.p: *Australian bonds starts the week firm as the market geared up for this week's inflation and wages data, shrugging off the softer tone in U.S. Treasuries late last week.
*TCV to hold A$100 million bond tender at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
Australian bonds started the week firm as the market geared up for this week's second quarter inflation and wages data, shrugging off the softer tone in U.S. Treasuries late last week.
"What you are seeing is a traditional run-up to the data, but I wouldn't expect to see a lot of business going through today," said one trader noting today's holiday in Japan.
Wednesday's second quarter inflation report is expected to show a 0.1 percent fall in the headline CPI for an annual rate of just 0.5 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
More importantly, the policy-sensitive underlying inflation rate is seen rising 0.4 percent for a 1.7 percent annual rate and below the Reserve Bank's 2.0 to 3.0 percent target.

Thursday's second quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings data are also seen being positive for the market, keeping the possibility of an easing in monetary policy to the fore with forecasts centring on a 0.8 percent rise.
This would give an annual rate of 4.1 percent and below the central bank's 4.5 percent 'line in the sand'.
A tentative rebound in the Australian dollar above US$0.7400 also aided the local positive tone.

Yield spreads to the U.S. narrowed sharply in advance of what is expected to bond friendly local data and as U.S. Treasuries showed signs of jitters on Friday ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony. Greenspan's two-day address starts on Tuesday.
